pageCache.pageTitle: Careers and Guidance - The Costello School
pageCache.text:
Careers and Guidance
Every child should leave school prepared for life in modern Britain. This means ensuring academic rigour supported by excellent teaching, and developing in every young person the values, skills and behaviours they need to get on in life. All children should receive a rich provision of classroom and extra-curricular activities that develop a range of character attributes, such as resilience and grit, which underpin success in education and employment. High quality, independent careers guidance is also crucial in helping pupils emerge from school more fully rounded and ready for the world of work. Young people want and need to be well-informed when making subject and career decisions.
Mr J HulseAssistant Headteacher/Careers Contact

pageCache.pageTitle: Report an Absence - The Costello School
pageCache.text:
Report an Absence
It is a legal requirement that your child attends school regularly. Excellent attendance is vital to students achieving their potential and, as a school, we place the highest importance on students being present and punctual. We expect students to achieve as close to 100% attendance as possible.
When your child is unwell you must inform the school on the first morning of absence and, for safeguarding purposes, provide daily updates. Medical certification must be provided for any illness exceeding 5 days. To report an absence please do this via Classcharts. Click here for a guide to support with this.
Please refer to NHS guidance on common conditions on the ‘Healthier Together’ poster – download here.
We ask that where possible you do not book routine medical appointments during the school day. Where this is not possible please ensure that your child attends school both before and /or after the appointment time as applicable.
For any planned absence you must submit a Leave of Absence Request Form in good time. Click here for the form– please return it to the school reception.
If you take your child on holiday, it will be recorded as unauthorised absence in all circumstances, and Penalty Notices will be issues in accordance with Hampshire County Council’s Code of Conduct.
Ten or more sessions of unauthorised absence in any 100 session period will result in a Penalty Notice of £60 per parent per child.
Students should aim to arrive at school no later than 8.30am (first bell), and they must be at their tutor room no later than 8.35am. If your child is late they will receive a detention.
Attendance Monitoring
You will receive an attendance letter at least twice a year, which will be colour-coded as follows;
Please do not hesitate to email our Attendance Officer Ms Southard s.southard@costello.hants.sch.uk

Hi, my name is Angus Haldane, and I am currently in Year 11. I’m a member of the Senior Student Leadership Team, as Head Student, and also a Cadet Corporal in the school’s Combined Cadet Force. As part of the leadership team, I was given the opportunity to meet the Mayor of Basingstoke when he attended the school to unveil Edith Weston’s Blue Plaque. I also recently represented the CCF contingent as part of Basingstoke’s annual Remembrance Day Parade, leading from the front and Basingstoke’s 80th anniversary of VE Day, calling the parade commands. Outside of school, I am an Explorer Scout, and a young leader attached a local Cub Scout Group. I am also a member of BATS Net Gen, the youth section of the Basingstoke Amateur Theatrical Society, and have recently enjoyed roles in some of their most recent productions; Little Shop of Horrors, Sponge Bob the Musical, Cats and Everybody’s Talking About Jamie. When not on stage or on parade I enjoy spending time with my friends, family and my dog Toby on walks in the local countryside.

I am currently a Year 10 student and additionally a member of the Student Leadership team. Before becoming a Deputy Head Student, I have had the joy and privilege of being a House Captain. I am also an Anti-Bullying Ambassador, which I have been since Year 7.
I have previously been a part of many events such as giving speeches at an award ceremony and also a speech at an open evening in my first year, I have met many individuals through the school such as Cllr Paul Harvey, MP Luke Murphy, former Mayor of Basingstoke Cllr Paul Miller, the current Mayor Cllr Colin Phillimore and Deputy Mayor Cllr Jacky Tustain.
I have had the pleasure of participating in the School’s production of Matilda and also Beauty and the Beast, where I was in the crew as an audio engineer.
Outside of school I am involved in politics. I have a lot planned for the year ahead, which I am deeply looking forward too. I enjoy spending time with my Pug Bailey, my 2 goats Conan and Doyle and my family.

My name is Isabelle and I am extremely proud to be a part of the Student Senior Leadership Team.
Before becoming a Deputy Head Student, I have been a part of many student representative groups such as the Student Voice and our Young Interpreter team. Additionally, I have served as a House Captain and Vice-Chairperson of the Eco Committee.
Beyond the school environment, I am passionate about the performing arts and I have been involved in many stage productions some of which are Peter Pan, Addams Family, Guys and Dolls, We Will Rock You and a West End variety show. I have also achieved a Grade 5 LAMDA acting distinction. Moreover, I have been a part of Costello’s productions of Matilda, Beauty and the Beast and Grease the musical which has helped many students build confidence and express themselves in a supportive, engaging environment.
Outside of performing, I enjoy spending time with my family and friends and reading.
I take pride in being a student at Costello and being part of a community which encourages each and every student to achieve their full potential both academically and through their hobbies and interests.
I look forward to continuing to support the Student Leadership team with my role in external communications and ensuring that every student feels valued and included within our school.
Isabelle

Keerthana
Outside of school, I have been passionate about Bharatanatyam (Indian dance form) since Year 5, dedicating myself to this classical art form. Currently, I am enrolled in the Grade 9 (Post-Diploma) course with Nupura School of Arts, having successfully completed my Grade 3 exam. Performing Bharatanatyam has been a fulfilling experience, enabling me to share […]
Outside of school, I have been passionate about Bharatanatyam (Indian dance form) since Year 5, dedicating myself to this classical art form. Currently, I am enrolled in the Grade 9 (Post-Diploma) course with Nupura School of Arts, having successfully completed my Grade 3 exam. Performing Bharatanatyam has been a fulfilling experience, enabling me to share this rich tradition with others and grow both as a dancer and an individual.
I performed Bharatanatyam at the Basingstoke Variety Show, it was a very proud moment to represent my cultural heritage on such a platform. Additionally, I received an award from the Mayor for my contribution to raising funds for the Mayor’s charity appeal.
In school, I played a key role in organising events such as the production of the musical Matilda Jr. and a joyful festival of Eisteddfod by managing backstage operations ensuring everything ran seamlessly behind the scenes.
I was honoured to achieve the position of deputy head student, where I work with both students and staff to foster positive and supportive environment. The Senior Management Team has been incredibly supportive in guiding me and helping to contribute effectively to school initiatives and student engagement.
Keerthana

Ellie

I am currently in Year 10 and a Deputy Head student here at Costello.
In my free time I am an Explorer Scout, and part of the Combined Cadet Force here at Costello. I enjoy the arts and I strongly believe that subjects like these are an essential part of education. Before becoming part of the Senior Student Leadership Team, I achieved my gold award in Scouting and was part of the Student Voice. As well as Explorers, outside of school I do dance and enjoy baking, hiking and spending time with my friends. Last year I was part of the school production of Beauty and the Beast, this meant I was able to meet loads of new people and make some very close friends.
I’m incredibly proud to be a part of the Costello Community and I will strive to make our school a place that students look forward to coming to every day.

Michaela
I am a Deputy Head Student at Costello and I am currently in Year 9. I enjoy art and reading and this year I am taking part in the school’s production as part of the backstage team. Through school, I have completed my Bronze Duke of Edinburgh Expedition and participated in the Combined Cadet Force. […]
I am a Deputy Head Student at Costello and I am currently in Year 9. I enjoy art and reading and this year I am taking part in the school’s production as part of the backstage team. Through school, I have completed my Bronze Duke of Edinburgh Expedition and participated in the Combined Cadet Force. In the past I have participated in scouting and I help the local community. I especially love the arts program at Costello because I find that many people enjoy working together and I believe that this helps our community here at Costello.
Michaela

Paige
I am a Year 11 student here at Costello and whilst I am currently a head student, I have previously been a house captain and helped contribute to various events including the colour run and sports day. I’ve also participated in the first Eisteddfod performance we had here at Costello, playing my cello which I […]
I am a Year 11 student here at Costello and whilst I am currently a head student, I have previously been a house captain and helped contribute to various events including the colour run and sports day.
I’ve also participated in the first Eisteddfod performance we had here at Costello, playing my cello which I have been doing since Year 3. I am currently working towards my Grade 6.
Outside of school I do Taekwondo – I am now a black belt, having been working towards it for over 10 years.
I also love drawing and I am really passionate about the value of the arts in education and hope to incorporate that more in our school in my time as head student.

Headteacher’s Welcome
Welcome to The Costello School.
Our values of Enjoy, Respect and Achieve run through everything we do. They shape our culture, our decisions and our ambition to develop the ‘Game-Changers’ of the future. We are conscious every day of the trust placed in us, and we are ambitious for every pupil to leave us confident, resilient and ready to take their place in the world.
At Costello, pupils learn in a calm, purposeful environment where they feel safe, behave very well and are able to focus on their learning. Strong relationships between staff and pupils, alongside clear and consistent expectations, ensure that learning is rarely disrupted and that every pupil is supported to succeed.
We are proud to offer a broad and ambitious experience for all pupils. Whether students aspire to university, have talents in sport or the arts, or pursue vocational pathways, we ensure that every individual is known, supported and challenged. Opportunities such as trips, enrichment and our outdoor curriculum help pupils to develop confidence, character and a strong sense of belonging.
As a larger school, we are able to offer a wide range of facilities and opportunities, while maintaining a strong sense of community where every pupil is valued as an individual.
I warmly encourage you to visit us during the school day. Our pupils are proud of their school and will be delighted to show you what it means to be part of the Costello community.

Click here for more information or fill in the form to register your interest here.
Each Bohunt school has a local governing board which reports directly to the Bohunt trust board on a regular basis. Governors carry out key functions in supporting schools, working closely with headteachers to:
The local governing board offers strategic support and guidance to school leaders enabling young people to fulfil their potential and achieve their aspirations. They consistently challenge processes and drive continuous school improvement having a significant role in the long-term development and improvement of the school and provide strong links with the wider community.
If you would like to contact the Local Governing Board, or are interested in being a governor at a BET school, please email the Trust Governance Lead at staylor1@bohunt.hants.sch.uk

Enrichment Opportunities
We firmly believe in the value of enriched learning outside of the classroom and we organise a wide range of trips, expeditions and visits; locally, nationally and internationally. These range in length from a half day field visit, perhaps to Festival Place, to week in the Alps skiing. They also include sporting fixtures, adventurous activities and recreational activities.
Whilst costs are kept to a minimum the school is reliant on voluntary contributions to cover the costs of trips; sometimes trips have to be cancelled if there are insufficient voluntary contributions to fund the costs of the trip. No child is restricted from taking part through an individual inability to pay. For more information please contact the Finance Team.
All of our trips and visits are organised under the guidance framework recommended by Hampshire Local Authority.
